newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Lost Asian refugees detained up in Slovakia.
newsitem.headline: Lost Asian refugees detained up in Slovakia.

text.p: Slovak border police have detained a group of 143 refugees, including 46 children, who were fooled into thinking they were in Germany, the Interior Ministry said on Thursday.
The group of 90 Afghans, 46 Iraqi Kurds and seven Sri Lankans, was discovered after four refugees arrived at the Cerveny Kamen border crossing in western Slovakia, and asked for political asylum.

Interior Ministry Spokesman Norbert Lazar told Reuters the refugees did not know where they were, nor how they had got there, other than the fact that they had travelled for several days both by air and road.
"They had obviously been duped," Lazar said. "They were driven down to the border by their traffickers, pointed in the direction of the border and told they would be in Germany."
He said seven children and one woman had immediately been taken to hospital suffering from third degree frostbite.
Lazar added it was probable that the entire group would apply for political asylum in Slovakia.
